answer.rationale: Judged strictly on the distance between what each memory actually measured and the objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue), plus what each omits. memory_57 is strongest (4): it is the only entry that names qualified revenue AND checks a durability guardrail (retention); it still omits effect size, incentive cost/margin, and whether the referred accounts were incremental. memory_44 (3) reports pipeline quality, a genuine qualification proxy, but stops short of closed-won revenue, cycle length, or retention. memory_73 (2) claims acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about margin, discount depth, post-promo renewal, or whether the acquired accounts were qualified — discount-driven revenue is exactly the kind that can be non-sustainable, and it is the memory most likely to be misread as a ready answer to the competitor's entry pricing. memory_31 (2) and memory_86 (2) measure activation/onboarding completion only; both are upstream proxies with no revenue link, and both involve removing friction (fewer signup fields, shorter onboarding) in ways that could plausibly reduce lead qualification or depth of setup — a tradeoff neither memory tested. memory_91 is weakest (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the most proximal, most easily inflated metrics in the set, with no retention, conversion, or revenue follow-through at all. Cross-cutting caveats: every entry is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so none can be re-audited; none report sample size, effect magnitude, duration, control design, or segment boundaries; and all predate the current quarter's declines (newest is day 61, oldest day 12), so any of them may have decayed or been invalidated by the competitor's entry. The current activation (-6%) and onboarding (-4%) declines are themselves evidence that the conditions behind memory_31, memory_86, and memory_91 have shifted. I would not treat any of these as a decision-ready basis for this week's single slot without asking what the archived sources actually showed.
